name: EPIK (English Program in Korea)
operator: National Institute for International Education (NIIE), Korean Ministry of Education
summary: Korean government program placing native English speakers as co-teachers in public elementary, middle and high schools nationwide. Salaried position with free furnished housing, entrance and exit allowances, and national health insurance.
other_eligibility: Passport from USA, UK, Ireland, Canada, Australia, New Zealand or South Africa. Bachelor's degree (any field, apostilled). 100+ hour TEFL/TESOL/CELTA with tutor-graded component required for Level 2 pay; Level 3 (degree only) is effectively not hired by any provincial office. Apostilled national criminal background check; medical exam after arrival. E-2 visa.
pay_note: Base monthly salary by level and province: roughly KRW 2,100,000-2,800,000, with Seoul (SMOE) top grade and Chungbuk S+ reaching KRW 3,000,000. On top of base: entrance allowance KRW 1,300,000-1,800,000 (first contract only), contract completion bonus KRW 1,300,000-1,800,000, settlement allowance KRW 300,000 on arrival, rural/multi-school allowances KRW 100,000-150,000/month. US citizens may be exempt from Korean income tax for the first two years under the US-Korea tax treaty.

deadlines.note: Online application opened 1 Aug 2026 09:00 KST. EPIK reviews on a rolling basis in the order received; strong candidates should apply in the first weeks.
Cycle expected to close around November 2026, but EPIK closes early once places fill. No fixed published cutoff date.

caveat_note: EPIK is free to apply to directly, but many applicants go through recruiters (Korvia, Gone2Korea, etc.) - recruiters are free to the applicant and paid by EPIK, so never pay a recruiter. Salary level is assigned by EPIK, not chosen: a plain bachelor's with no TEFL lands at Level 3, which no provincial office actually hires, so the practical floor for a US applicant is Level 2 (KRW ~2.1-2.3M) and requires a 100+ hour tutor-graded TEFL. Housing is free but small and utilities are not covered. E-2 visa requires apostilled degree and FBI background check, which takes months. Verification note: epik.go.kr would not load (TLS certificate error), so salary and deadline figures come from Korvia, a major EPIK recruiter, cross-checked against esl.careers - not from the ministry directly.

name: Taiwan Foreign English Teacher Program (TFETP)
operator: Ministry of Education (Taiwan), K-12 Education Administration
summary: Taiwan's government program placing foreign English teachers (FETs) and teaching assistants (FETAs) in public elementary and junior high schools nationwide under a co-teaching model with local Taiwanese teachers. Salaried, with airfare reimbursement, housing reimbursement and insurance.
other_eligibility: Passport from a country where English is an official or commonly used language, as recognized by Taiwan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Bachelor's degree or higher, majority not earned by distance learning. Nationwide criminal background check. FET track additionally requires a state-issued teaching license, or 1+ year of English teaching experience at an accredited school, or an accredited TESOL/TEFL/CELTA certificate.
pay_note: Two distinct tracks. Foreign English Teaching Assistant (FETA): flat NT$45,000/month. Foreign English Teacher (FET) with a bachelor's degree: NT$62,720-78,045/month; master's NT$69,965-86,820; doctorate NT$73,025-91,420. Also airfare reimbursement, housing reimbursement, insurance, and professional development funding. FETs additionally get performance bonuses and spouse/relative airfare reimbursement; FETAs get TESOL/TEFL/CELTA certification reimbursement and transport allowances. 980 positions budgeted for the 2026 recruitment round.

deadlines.note: Applications are open now via tfetp.k12ea.gov.tw with rolling review and interviews until all positions fill. Recruitment for August starts typically runs January-April (an April 30 cutoff has been cited in past cycles); for February starts, September-November.

caveat_note: The headline NT$62,720+ figure is the FET track, which requires a teaching license, prior classroom experience, or a TEFL certificate - a plain BA with none of those routes you to the FETA track at NT$45,000/month, a materially different offer. Housing is reimbursed or subsidized (commonly NT$5,000-10,000/month), not free-and-furnished as some third-party marketing implies. Salary tiers here are from Taiwan MOE-derived third-party summaries; the official portal did not render for direct verification, so confirm exact figures on tfetp.k12ea.gov.tw before relying on them.

name: HESS Educational Organization - Taiwan
operator: HESS International Educational Group (private buxiban chain)
summary: Taiwan's largest private English-language school chain, hiring foreign teachers year-round on 12-month contracts for after-school kindergarten and elementary programs. No placement fee; HESS handles work permit and ARC paperwork and provides orientation and training.
other_eligibility: Bachelor's or associate degree plus a TEFL (or equivalent) certificate; no prior experience required. Taiwan work permits for buxiban teaching in practice require a passport from a designated English-speaking country (US, UK, Canada, Ireland, Australia, NZ, South Africa) and a bachelor's degree, or an associate degree paired with a TEFL certificate. Criminal background check and health check required.
pay_note: NT$680-730 per teaching hour to start, with annual performance raises of up to NT$40/teaching hour. Additional NT$3,000/month for non-teaching duties (prep, grading). Guaranteed minimum 20 teaching hours/week; most teachers work 22-26. New teachers typically gross NT$60,000-70,000/month all-in. Contract completion bonus paid at the end of the 12 months. Note: pay is per TEACHING hour, not per hour on site - unpaid prep, meetings and admin time are real and reduce the effective hourly rate.

deadlines.note: HESS hires year-round; arrival and start date are negotiated at interview.

caveat_note: HESS charges the teacher no placement fee, but you must arrive with cash: HESS itself tells applicants to bring roughly US$2,000 because the first paycheck lands about seven weeks after arrival. Housing is not provided - HESS helps you look during orientation, and an optional interest-free NT$30,000 startup loan is offered, repaid over six months out of salary. Only 12-month contracts are available and breaking one has visa/ARC consequences. Hourly rate figures are from HESS recruiting listings and third-party TEFL sites; the official FAQ confirms hours, contract length and eligibility but does not publish the rate.

name: Fulbright Austria US Teaching Assistantship (USTA)
operator: Fulbright Austria (Austrian-American Educational Commission), funded by the Austrian Federal Ministry of Education
summary: Places American college graduates as English teaching assistants in Austrian secondary schools for one school year, employed and paid by the Austrian Ministry of Education. Despite the Fulbright branding it is administered separately from the Fulbright US Student Program and has its own application and deadline.
other_eligibility: US citizenship (dual US citizens eligible). Bachelor's degree completed by the program start, or final-year student at time of application. German proficiency of at least B1 (CEFR) / Intermediate Mid (ACTFL) is a hard requirement - applicants below it cannot be considered. 13 contact hours per week.
pay_note: Approximately EUR 2,012 gross per month, roughly EUR 1,631 net after Austrian tax and social insurance. Health and accident coverage through BVAEB is mandatory and included. Fulbright Austria states plainly that the monthly salary is the only money you receive in connection with the job - the low figure here is net, the high figure is gross, not a range of offers.

deadlines.note: Applications accepted only between 15 Nov 2026 and 15 Jan 2027. Program starts 1 October 2027 with orientation in late September.

caveat_note: Two things the marketing understates. First, no relocation allowance and no housing: you pay your own airfare and find and fund your own apartment in Austria, which is a real cash-flow problem before the first paycheck. Second, the contract runs 1 October to 31 May only - about eight months - so budget for the gap on either end. It is also not a Fulbright grant despite the name, so it does not carry Fulbright alumni status or the Fulbright US Student Program deadline; the separate January deadline catches people out.

name: Central European Teaching Program (CETP) - Hungary
operator: Central European Teaching Program (private US-based placement organization)
summary: Places English speakers as full-time teachers in Hungarian state schools, mostly in small towns, on the same local pay scale as Hungarian teachers with housing and utilities covered by the host school. CETP charges the participant an upfront placement fee even though the school pays a salary.
other_eligibility: Bachelor's degree. TEFL/TESOL certification preferred but not universally required. Native or near-native English. Criminal background check. CETP sponsors the residence permit; because of its agreement with Hungary no Hungarian government permit fees are charged. Participants must buy their own travel insurance before arrival.
pay_note: Paid in Hungarian forint on the same public pay scale as local Hungarian teachers - CETP does not publish a figure. Third-party TEFL sites estimate roughly EUR 500-700/month net equivalent, which is enough to live on locally but leaves almost no savings. Teaching load is 22-26 contact hours per week. Full Hungarian national health coverage and paid school holidays included.
cost_note: Program fee, paid in USD: $2,500 for a full school year (Sept-June), $2,200 for a single semester, $1,000 to extend into years 2-5. Cancellation fee $700. Fee covers placement, housing and utilities arranged by the school, health insurance and residence permit processing, airport pickup and in-country orientation. International airfare is NOT included.

deadlines.note: Rolling admissions. Full-year placements start with Budapest orientation around 21-22 August and run September to mid-June; mid-year placements run January to June.

caveat_note: This is the clearest fee-and-salary hybrid on this list: you pay CETP $2,500 up front AND the Hungarian school pays you a local salary. CETP is candid about why - it receives no institutional or school funding - but a reader skimming 'paid full-time teaching placement' can easily miss the fee. The salary is a genuine Hungarian public-sector teacher wage, meaning it is low in absolute terms; do not model this as a money-making year. Placements are assigned, often in small towns with little English spoken, and CETP does not publish the salary figure anywhere, so ask for the specific forint amount for your assigned school before paying.

name: Fulbright English Teaching Assistant Award - Indonesia
operator: US Department of State / IIE, with AMINEF (American Indonesian Exchange Foundation) in-country
summary: Twenty ETAs are placed in Indonesian secondary schools, mostly in rural and peri-urban areas, for the 2027-28 academic year. Applications go through IIE on the national Fulbright timeline, not to AMINEF directly.
other_eligibility: US citizen; dual citizens of Indonesia are ineligible. Bachelor's or master's diploma in hand by June 2027. Cannot have resided in Indonesia during the year before the grant. Dependents may not accompany the grantee. Novice Indonesian recommended, not required. Teaching experience recommended.
pay_note: USD 700/month base stipend, plus a $100/month teaching allowance and a $100/month internet data allowance (each up to 8 months). One-time payments: $2,500 housing deposit, $500 relocation, $500 repatriation, $200 inoculations. International travel benefits included.
funding_note: Listed as open for the 2027-28 competition as of August 2026.

deadlines.note: National Fulbright deadline. Applicants still enrolled at a US university must meet their own campus deadline, typically 3-6 weeks earlier.

caveat_note: Placements are explicitly in rural and peri-urban areas with limited amenities and housing arranged by the host school - this is not a city posting. No dependents allowed. AMINEF is the in-country commission but does NOT accept applications; everything routes through IIE. Grant runs Aug 2027-May 2028, so the pay stops in May.

name: Fulbright English Teaching Assistant Award - Brazil
operator: US Department of State / IIE, with the Fulbright Commission Brazil
summary: Ten ETAs are placed in pairs at Brazilian public universities as language teaching assistants, working about 30 hours per week including planning. The 2027-28 cohort is Fulbright Brazil's 70th.
other_eligibility: Bachelor's or master's degree. One to two years of tutoring or classroom teaching experience with young adults is REQUIRED, not preferred. Advanced Portuguese (roughly three years of college-level study) or advanced Spanish plus some Portuguese study; a Foreign Language Evaluation form is mandatory. Cannot have resided in Brazil 3+ months in the year before the grant.
pay_note: USD 1,020/month, disbursed quarterly in $3,060 installments rather than monthly - budget for the lag. International travel benefits included.
funding_note: Listed as open for the 2027-28 competition as of August 2026.

deadlines.note: National Fulbright deadline. Campus deadlines for enrolled students are earlier.

caveat_note: Brazil is one of the more demanding ETA countries: advanced Portuguese and prior teaching experience are both hard requirements, which rules out most straight-out-of-college applicants. The grant does not start until March 2028 and runs only 8 months - a full year and a half after the October 2026 deadline, which is a long gap to plan around. No housing is provided; the Commission only makes introductions.

name: Fulbright English Teaching Assistant Award - Morocco
operator: US Department of State / IIE, with MACECE (Moroccan-American Commission for Educational and Cultural Exchange)
summary: Twelve ETAs teach English in Moroccan institutions for a full ten-month academic year, late August 2027 to early July 2028. One of the better-paid ETA postings relative to local cost of living.
other_eligibility: US citizen; dual citizens of Morocco ARE eligible. Bachelor's, master's or doctoral degree. Some relevant teaching experience is required and TESOL certification is strongly preferred; preference goes to master's holders with substantial classroom experience. Novice Arabic or French recommended. Cannot have lived in Morocco 6+ months in the year before the grant.
pay_note: Estimated USD 1,500/month, explicitly subject to change. International travel benefits included. Degree fields preferred: English, American Studies, Middle East Studies, Arabic, French, Education, TESOL or applied linguistics.
funding_note: Listed as open for the 2027-28 competition as of August 2026.

deadlines.note: National Fulbright deadline. Campus deadlines for enrolled students are earlier.

caveat_note: Teaching experience is a stated requirement and TESOL certification is strongly preferred, so this is not an entry-level ETA. Grantees find and pay for their own housing; MACECE provides city guides and alumni contacts only. The $1,500 stipend is marked as an estimate subject to change - confirm before signing. This is a MENA posting and US State Department travel guidance should be checked at application time.

name: Fulbright English Teaching Assistant Award - Jordan
operator: US Department of State / IIE, with the Jordanian-American Commission for Educational Exchange
summary: Twelve ETAs assist in teaching EFL at Jordanian educational institutions for a fixed nine-month term aligned to the Jordanian academic year. The highest monthly stipend of any ETA country reviewed here.
other_eligibility: US citizenship required. Bachelor's, master's or doctoral degree. At least one year of documentable in-classroom teaching experience is mandatory. Intermediate Arabic highly recommended but not required.
pay_note: USD 2,250/month total: $2,000 monthly maintenance allowance plus $250 monthly transportation allowance. Plus a one-time $1,500 relocation allowance for settling in. One-way airfare to Amman and airport transfer covered by the Commission, along with a 3-4 night hotel stay on arrival.
funding_note: Listed as open for the 2027-28 competition as of August 2026.

deadlines.note: National Fulbright deadline. Campus deadlines for enrolled students are earlier.

caveat_note: One full year of documented in-classroom teaching experience is a hard gate - this is not open to a graduating senior with no teaching history. The nine-month term is fixed with no adjustments. Housing is self-arranged after a short hotel stay; the $1,500 relocation allowance is meant to cover that. Airfare is one-way to Amman, not round-trip. Check current US State Department regional travel guidance at application time.

name: Fulbright English Teaching Assistant Award - Czech Republic
operator: US Department of State / IIE, with the Czech Fulbright Commission
summary: Twenty-five ETAs are placed as assistant teachers in Czech secondary schools in small and mid-sized towns outside the major cities, teaching 15-20 hours a week for the full ten-month school year. The largest ETA cohort of the European programs reviewed.
other_eligibility: US citizen; dual citizens of the Czech Republic are eligible. Bachelor's or master's degree by the award start date; PhD holders ineligible. Currently enrolled undergraduates and graduate students may apply. Czech language not required. Cannot have resided in the Czech Republic 3+ months in the year before the grant.
pay_note: CZK 35,000/month, pegged by the Commission to the average starting salary of a Czech high school teacher. International travel benefits included. Grant period begins with a 4-day ETA orientation in Liblice near Prague, plus a 3-day September orientation in Prague, a February mid-year conference and a farewell meeting.
funding_note: Listed as open for the 2027-28 competition as of August 2026.

deadlines.note: National Fulbright deadline. Campus deadlines for enrolled students are earlier.

caveat_note: The stipend is deliberately set at a Czech teacher's starting salary, not a US-expat salary - CZK 35,000/month is livable in a small Czech town and tight in Prague, and placements are specifically outside the big cities. Housing is not provided: most ETAs rent private apartments with help from the Commission and host school, though some schools offer dormitory rooms. PhD holders are barred.

name: Fulbright English Teaching Assistant Award - Poland
operator: US Department of State / IIE, with the Polish-US Fulbright Commission
summary: Nine ETAs are placed at Polish host institutions from October 2027 to June 2028, with university-provided accommodation covered by the host. Master's and doctoral students are explicitly preferred.
other_eligibility: US citizen. Bachelor's, master's or doctoral degree; master's and doctoral candidates preferred. Polish citizens holding green cards are ineligible. Polish language not required; novice level recommended.
pay_note: Stipend set at USD 1,200/month but disbursed in Polish zloty at the average USD/PLN exchange rate, so the zloty amount you actually receive floats with the exchange rate. One-time travel allowance of $1,500. Accommodation in a student dormitory or university staff house/hotel - individual room with bathroom access - is provided and paid by the host institution.
funding_note: Listed as open for the 2027-28 competition as of August 2026.

deadlines.note: National Fulbright deadline. Campus deadlines for enrolled students are earlier.

caveat_note: Only nine awards, and the Commission states a preference for master's and doctoral candidates - a fresh BA is a long shot here. The stipend is denominated in USD but paid in PLN, so a weak dollar cuts your real purchasing power mid-grant. Housing is genuinely covered but is dormitory or staff-hotel accommodation, not an apartment. Poles holding US green cards are specifically excluded.

name: CIEE Teach Abroad
summary: CIEE places participants in paid teaching roles in South Korea, Thailand and Spain (plus a summer program in Dublin), charging a program fee on top of the host-paid salary or stipend. CIEE has announced it is retiring its current Teach Abroad programs beginning in 2027.
other_eligibility: Bachelor's degree required for the Korea and Thailand placements (visa requirement). TEFL certification is sold as an optional paid add-on rather than included. Country-specific visa, background check and document legalization requirements apply.
pay_note: Compensation varies by destination and CIEE does not publish a single figure; individual country pages now redirect to the index, so nothing could be confirmed at source. Reported figures: Thailand roughly THB 30,000-43,000/month plus free furnished accommodation; Spain roughly EUR 1,000/month stipend plus orientation lodging and local health insurance; South Korea a salaried public-school placement with free housing. Treat all of these as unverified.
cost_note: Program fee reported at roughly USD 2,000 for a year-long placement, varying by country and option; TEFL certification is an additional paid add-on. CIEE does not publish fees on the public site and directs enquiries to teach@ciee.org or 207-274-5783. Figure is unverified.
funding_note: CIEE has announced it will retire its current Teach Abroad programs beginning in 2027, citing a changing business environment. The Teach in Spain Volunteer program is suspended beginning Fall 2026, and new TEFL certification programs were suspended beginning June 2026. Country program pages are already redirecting to the index page, suggesting the wind-down is underway.

deadlines.note: Historically rolling with fall and spring intakes, but with the program retiring from 2027 the intake calendar is unreliable. Contact CIEE directly before planning around it.

caveat_note: This is the archetypal both-directions program: CIEE charges you a placement fee AND the host school pays you a salary, so it is neither a pure job nor a pure fee program. More important for a 2026-27 directory: CIEE has publicly announced it is retiring Teach Abroad beginning in 2027 and has already suspended the Spain volunteer track and new TEFL certifications. The Thailand and Spain program pages are dead links that 301 to the landing page. Do not list this as a reliable option for a 2027 start without confirming directly with CIEE.

name: Thailand Government School English Teaching (OBEC public schools)
operator: Thai Ministry of Education public schools (OBEC), hired directly or via private placement agencies
summary: Thai government primary and secondary schools hire foreign English teachers year-round, most commonly for the May and November semester intakes. There is no single centralized Thai government recruitment program for foreigners - hiring is school-by-school or through fee-charging private placement providers.
other_eligibility: Bachelor's degree in any field (required for the work permit). TEFL/TESOL certificate, typically 120 hours, effectively required. Clean criminal background check. Non-Immigrant B visa, work permit, and a Teacher's License Waiver from the Teachers' Council of Thailand. Degree and background check usually need notarization and legalization.
pay_note: Government/public schools typically pay THB 25,000-40,000/month, with THB 30,000 the common baseline for a degree-plus-TEFL first-timer and up to ~THB 43,000-45,000 for stronger qualifications or bilingual-program roles. Housing is sometimes free or subsidized (a THB 3,000/month housing allowance is common at bilingual schools) but is not standard at ordinary government schools. Private bilingual and international schools pay considerably more but are a different hiring track.
cost_note: No cost if hired directly by a school. Placement providers (XploreAsia, CIEE, and similar) charge roughly USD 1,000-2,500 for orientation, in-country TEFL and placement - a real cost that varies by provider and is not reflected here.

deadlines.note: Rolling. Thai school year has two intakes: the main term starts mid-May and the second term starts early November. Most positions are advertised 6-8 weeks ahead to allow work-permit processing.

caveat_note: The biggest misconception: there is no Thai government program that recruits Americans the way JET or EPIK do. What exists is a hiring market, and most first-timers reach it through private placement companies that charge USD 1,000-2,500 - which is a cost, not a salary deduction, and is frequently blurred in marketing that describes these as 'paid programs.' Going direct to a school is free but requires being in Thailand or working a network. Salary figures here are aggregated from TEFL industry sources rather than an official OBEC pay schedule; verify the specific school's offer. Working on a tourist visa is common and illegal - insist on the Non-B visa and work permit.

name: Vietnam Public School English Teaching
operator: Vietnamese public schools and provincial Departments of Education and Training, usually contracted through language-center partners
summary: Vietnamese public schools in Hanoi, Ho Chi Minh City and the provinces hire foreign English teachers, generally through language centers that hold the school contract rather than by direct government recruitment. Among the higher-paying entry-level teaching markets in Southeast Asia relative to cost of living.
other_eligibility: Bachelor's degree in any subject, physically authenticated by the Vietnamese embassy in your home country. 120-hour TEFL certificate from a recognized provider, also legalized. Clean criminal background check, legalized. Business visa plus work permit; teaching on a tourist visa is illegal. Non-native speakers additionally need an English proficiency certificate such as IELTS.
pay_note: Roughly VND 30,000,000-40,000,000/month (about USD 1,150-1,550) is the standard band for public schools and language centers; some public-school roles are quoted at USD 1,495-2,050. A TEFL certificate typically adds VND 3-5 million/month. Some Hanoi public-school contracts are quoted hourly, up to VND 730,000/teaching hour with a guaranteed minimum of 60 teaching hours per month. Housing and airfare are not standard.
cost_note: No fee when hired directly or by a language center. Document legalization (degree, TEFL, background check) through the Vietnamese embassy is a real out-of-pocket cost of a few hundred dollars.

deadlines.note: Rolling year-round, with the heaviest hiring ahead of the September academic-year start. Positions are typically advertised 6-8 weeks in advance to allow work-permit processing.

caveat_note: There is no Vietnamese government teach-abroad program for Americans; 'Vietnam public school teaching' is a hiring market mediated by language centers that hold the school contract, so your employer is usually the center, not the school. The paperwork burden is the real obstacle: your physical degree, TEFL certificate and background check all have to be notarized and legalized through the Vietnamese embassy before you arrive, which takes months. Many teachers work initially on a business or tourist visa while the work permit processes; this is technically illegal and periodically enforced. Salary figures are from TEFL industry sources, not an official pay schedule.
